# run link100 wave 9c, lane DTORS2 -- THE WAVE-9c DESTRUCTOR FORWARDERS.
#
# Same shape as port/slice_dtors_a.txt and for the same reason: the rows below
# are the GENERATED FILE itself, not src translation units.  Every owning src TU
# is already compiled into walk_window; what the link is missing is a
# DEFINITION of the flat ROM destructor name, and no slice row can add one.
#
# TWO PREMISES, and port/tools/dtorfwd.py says which each row stands on.
#
#   BATCH 4, seven rows, DTORS-A's own premise.  The class header spells the
#   destructor inline; the forwarder's qualified call odr-uses it so MSVC emits
#   it.  Lane DTORS-A could not take these seven at 8dc06444f because their
#   owning TUs were not compiled then; lanes SEATS2 and HOSTGEN4 have seated
#   d_a_wanwan.cpp, daPkn_c.cpp and the three ov029 water TUs since, so they are
#   now ordinary inline-in-header rows.
#
#   BATCH 5, ten rows, the OUT-OF-LINE premise this lane adds.  The header only
#   DECLARES the destructor and the class's own per-function structor TU
#   (src/_ZN<n><Cls>D1Ev.cpp, on a live slice row) defines it, so
#   ??1<Cls>@@UAE@XZ is already in this link and the forwarder only CALLS it.
#   Read with dumpbin at 319f0f191, one object per class: ModelAnim,
#   TextureSequence, TextureTransformer, dCapEnemy_c, dScMgSnowball_c.
#   out/SEATS2/seat_table.md settles why compiling such a TU is not itself the
#   answer: a per-function structor TU does not define its own flat ROM name
#   under MSVC, so seating one never closed the row it was seated for.
#
# THE ROM-SIDE QUESTION IS THE SAME ONE either way, and it is asked the same
# way: port/tools/dtor_store_guard.py re-disassembles each cartridge body out of
# extracted/ in the pre-configure guard wave and refuses any class whose body
# dispatches through word 0 between the vtable store and the base restore.  The
# guard now reads D2 definitions as well as D0/D1, so a base-object destructor
# forwarder cannot slip past it unread.
#
# WALK_WINDOW ONLY, on port/slice_dtors_a.txt's rule: the wall these rows were
# measured against is walk_window's own unresolved block, and a definition that
# has not been measured on a target does not belong on it.
port/hal/dtor_forwarders_gen_w9c.cpp

# THE WRAPPER STRUCTORS, a different row shape in the same lane's file set.
# Four src TUs declare a small SharedFilePtr wrapper inside themselves with a
# constructor and a destructor DECLARED and neither DEFINED, and instantiate one
# at file scope, so walk_window asks for ??0<Cls>@@QAE@I@Z and ??1<Cls>@@QAE@XZ
# in MSVC's own spelling.  config/tu_manifest.d records which ROM address the
# cartridge resolved each of those imports to, with the relocation that proves
# it, and every one of those destinations is already defined in this link
# (hal/cxx_aliases.cpp's veneers and src/SharedFilePtr_Destruct_Clsn.c), so this
# file needs no seat and can add none.  No vtable question arises: neither
# SharedFilePtr nor any of the four wrappers declares a virtual.
port/hal/dtor_forwarders_gen_w9c_structors.cpp
